newsitem.title: USA: NYS McCall says state will pay $24 bln in interest.
newsitem.headline: NYS McCall says state will pay $24 bln in interest.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller, who has criticised Gov George Pataki for "backdoor" borrowing, Tuesday said it will cost taxpayers $24 billion in interest to repay the state's $31 billion of outstanding debt.

Saying the amount of debt that has not been approved by voters had shot up 57 percent since 1992 to more than $25 billion outstanding, State Comptroller H. Carl McCall faulted Albany lawmakers for failing to address how this affected the state's economy and its long-term growth.
A spokesman for the comptroller, a potential Democratic candidate for governor in next year's race, was not immediately available to explain over what time frame the debt would be repaid.
McCall said he expected to start updating the forecasts on a quarterly basis, as part of an effort to better inform taxpayers and bring them into a debate.

The Republican governor has proposed increasing non-voter approved debt by $2 billion, the state comptroller said, faulting this plan. "For years, the trend in this state has been to give the taxpayers less and less of a voice in how much state debt is issued through backdoor borrowing. This trend must be reversed."
The non-voter approved debt issued since 1992 has paid for a range of projects, including prisons, highways, bridges and environmental work, McCall said.
